label: DEMO: labelled pairs over corpus.json, and incoming saves that are compared with it. Every text is invented.

labels.duplicate: the same facts in the same scope, worded the same or differently: merging the two loses nothing. A save like this is blocked or flagged.
labels.near-duplicate: the same subject and scope with mostly the same facts, where one adds or drops a minor detail without contradicting the other: a merge candidate for review, never an automatic merge.
labels.contradiction: the same subject, with a fact that cannot be true at the same time as the other's (another day, number, choice or place). `resolved` says whether the corpus already settles it with a supersedes link and validity windows (true), or nothing does yet and a person must review it (false).
labels.related: different facts about the same thing, project, event or people, that a reader would want shown together or linked, whether or not the corpus links them.
labels.unrelated: no shared subject: a link would be wrong. `hard` marks pairs that share a word, a name or a topic and so tempt a similarity threshold.
labels.insight: an older and a newer stored record, written 30 or more days apart and readable together by one person, whose combination says something neither says alone (a consequence, a risk, a pattern); `why` says what.

rules: Each pair has exactly one label. When two could apply, the first of duplicate, near-duplicate, contradiction, insight, related, unrelated wins.
a is the earlier record and b the later: a memory by when it was created, a note by its last change, a document by its current revision, an incoming save by when it would be saved.
An incoming item is a save that has not happened yet. It is compared with what is stored and is never loaded into the corpus.
Duplicates and near-duplicates live in one scope: a copy in another scope is a share, not a duplicate.
A pair across Alex's and Sam's personal scopes is labelled by meaning, related or unrelated only. No engine may link, merge or compare it where either person would see the result.
An insight pair is two stored records that at least one person may read together.
Every supersession in the corpus is a resolved contradiction pair, and an unresolved one has no supersedes link.
Unrelated pairs have no link in the corpus.
hard marks a pair a similarity threshold is likely to get wrong: a shared word or name with another meaning, or one meaning in very different words.
